## The eager-path cost and the measured gap {#sec-ch11-s4}

### Summary

The eager step of the V3 code issues more device launches than the pre-V3 code did: kernels, copies and fills
that the new structure (the register, the status slots, the split stage) adds. On a GPU an eager step's cost
follows its launch count more than its arithmetic, so the eager step is slower than the pre-V3 eager step, and
the CUDA graph path, which replays a whole segment as one launch, is the remedy. The launch reductions made in the
kernels themselves are listed here by the code that carries them, and the section cites the record that measured
the gap and the bound ruled from it. It repeats none of the record's numbers.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Say what the eager path costs against the pre-V3 code, where the launch reductions are, and where the
measurement is recorded.

**Data.** None at run time; cites the S4 record (launches per step and milliseconds per step on four cells).

**Placement.** Outside the solver: a record on the closing-plan branch.

**Activation.** None.

**Guarantee / limits.** The bound as ruled: on CUDA the default execution is no slower per step than the pre-V3
eager code on every cell, and on the CPU the eager step is within 5 % of it; an explicit `execution: eager` on
CUDA is reported, not bounded.[^ch11-s4-src]

**Evidence.** The S4 record; no ctest at the pin (@tbl-ch11-s4-tests).
:::

Local symbols of this section: none.

### Derivation

None: a catalogue and a citation. The record compares three columns on each cell, measured in one session on one
build of each side: the pre-V3 code (eager only), the V3 code with no execution key, and the V3 code with
`execution: eager`. Its four cells are the Straka case with HLLC[^rg-150c5a646a54] in FP64, the shipped Straka deck, a six-panel
moist cubed sphere, and the same sphere with an implicit scheme and a varying step. Launches are counted from the
profiler trace by the method of @sec-ch16-launches; times are medians of repeated runs.[^ch11-s4-src]

### Numerical method

**Where the launches are reduced.** At the pin each reduction sits in the code it changes, which marks it "V3 S4"
in a comment. No chapter of this book describes them one by one, so the catalogue cites the code:

| what | code |
|---|---|
| the reconstruction floors and the Riemann events post masks (row, mask pairs), and the monitor reduces a stage's masks together: one integer cumulative sum and one gather per stage, no atomics | `floored` of {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.hpp ReconstructImpl >}}, `events` of {{< code src/riemann/riemann.hpp RiemannSolverImpl >}}, {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp RegisterMonitor::flush_counts >}} |
| the well-balanced $x_1$ fallback computes its positivity mask once and shares it | {{< code src/recon/well_balanced_x1.cpp >}} |
| the register's stage rates and posts stay in per-stage slots and are folded once, on the device, when the amounts are read; `end_stage` launches nothing | {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp RegisterMonitor::end_stage >}}, {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp RegisterMonitor::fold_ >}} |
| a contiguous row range is one plain add on a narrow view instead of an atomic `index_add_` | {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::add >}} |
| the prescribed-wall rates of a stage are booked in one batch for every register and direction | {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.hpp WallBatch >}} |
| the implicit solve's five status bits index a cached truth table: one gather and one reduction | {{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::status >}} |
| the implicit tracer transfer builds its shifted copies with one pad each, without a zero fill | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_advance >}} |

: The S4 catalogue: the eager-path launch reductions at the pin, by the code that carries them.
{#tbl-ch11-s4-catalogue}

**Why the graph path is the remedy.** The record reads its counts and times together: the eager gap is
launch-bound, as the times order the same way as the launch counts, and the graph path, which replays each
captured segment as one launch, runs every cell faster than the pre-V3 eager code.[^ch11-s4-src] This is why
`auto` resolves to cuda-graph on CUDA (@sec-ch11-default), rather than every remaining extra launch being removed
from the eager path.

### Code

**How to use it.** To see which path a run took, read its counters after a few steps:

```python
r = block.execution_report()
print(r["replays"], r["eager"])    # graph path: replays, no eager stage
```

**What is refused, and why.** Nothing: this section changes no code. The counting tool and the record are on the
closing-plan branch, not in the snapy tree at the pin.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The record's numbers belong to the commits it names, on the machines it names; this report cites them and does
  not re-measure them at its pin.
- Times on a shared node move with its load; the record says which of its tables were measured on an idle GPU.
- The eager path on CUDA has no bound: a case that runs eager there (a refusal, or `execution: eager`) pays the
  launch gap.
:::
